text:
Alex: FYI Paywise (dedicated pool id=paywise-prod-1) reported a sharp throughput drop ~60% and client 429s starting ~12:10UTC. They say autoscale never triggered. Pasting a small slice of our logs and their repro below.

Alex: Logs from their pool (snip):
```
[2026-03-17T12:09:58Z] pool=paywise-prod-1 queue_depth=128 continuous_batcher_pending=95 dispatched_batches=2 429_count=42
[2026-03-17T12:10:04Z] model=redwood-1 tokens_in_batch=4 avg_batch_size=2.3 gpu_util=18% latency_p50=340ms 429=7
[2026-03-17T12:10:12Z] autoscaler_decision=NO_SCALE reason="util_below_thresh" gpu_util=19% cpu_util=12%
```

Dana: Which model variant and traffic pattern? Are they sending lots of tiny requests or one big streaming job? Also tagging @Sam on the scheduler side.

Sam: I pulled metrics for paywise-prod-1. They were hammering the pool with many short requests (~20–60 tokens) at ~120 rps. Continuous-batcher shows high queued requests but low tokens-per-batch (avg ~3 tokens). Batcher config shows `wait_for_min_tokens=true` and `batch_timeout_ms=50`.

Sam: Hypothesis — scheduler waits for min tokens / timeout semantics are causing dispatchs to go out with tiny batches. Small batches blow up per-request overhead on GPU, so GPU utilization appears low -> autoscaler doesn't trigger because it uses GPU util, while throughput collapses and we hit per-tenant throttles. This explains 429s + NO_SCALE.

Priya: Autoscaler logs corroborate: there were repeated scale evaluations but each showed gpu_util < 22% so scaler suppressed. Meanwhile queue_depth was rising because dispatch rate couldn't keep up. The scaler's burst_protection feature also prevented quick scale because it saw under-utilization.

Alex: Customer repro (they ran this against their pool):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}' & done; wait
```
They say after ~15s they started to see 429s and latency spikes.

Dana: Can we validate with an internal repro that mimics many tiny requests? If yes, we can try toggling batcher params and a patch to autoscaler burst config.

Sam: I ran a quick internal repro against a staging pool with `-c 200` concurrent short requests. Reproduced the pattern: queue_depth climbs, avg_batch_tokens stays ~3, gpu_util ~20%, many micro-batches, low dispatch efficiency.

Sam: Immediate mitigation suggestions (hotfix):
- enable continuous_batching (if off)
- set `min_batch_tokens=1` and `max_wait_ms=8` (reduce wait time)
- lower `batcher_dispatch_interval_ms` to 5
- temporarily increase autoscaler "burst_capacity_override" for paywise-prod-1 so it can scale despite low util signals

Sam: Config patch I applied to paywise-prod-1 (hotfix):
```yaml
batcher:
  continuous: true
  min_batch_tokens: 1
  max_wait_ms: 8
  dispatch_interval_ms: 5
autoscaler:
  burst_capacity_override: 2
  evaluation_window_s: 30
```

ops-bot: Deployment `hotfix/2001234567-paywise-batcher` rolled out to pool paywise-prod-1 at 12:28UTC.

Alex: I notified Paywise support contact and asked them to run the same stress repro. Kept them on the line.

Priya: Post-hotfix metrics (12:29–12:35UTC):
```
queue_depth peak before=142 now=12
avg_batch_tokens before=3 now=28
gpu_util before=19% now=64%
429_count before=58 now=0
```

Sam: Confirmed recovery in internal metrics — dispatch efficiency improved, throughput back to expected. Autoscaler also started scaling as gpu_util increased.

Alex: Paywise confirmed throughput returned and their engineering lead said no further 429s. They asked for root cause write-up and a durable fix.

Dana: Next steps (action items):
- Sam/eng-runtime: add automatic detection for "small-request flood" pattern (high queue_depth + low tokens_per_batch) and auto-apply a conservative batcher tuning patch scoped to the pool (alert + dry-run).
- Priya/infra: revisit autoscaler signal set — consider combining dispatch throughput metric with gpu_util for scale decisions so small-batch storms don't suppress scaling.
- Alex: send summary + timeline to Paywise, include repro and hotfix details.

Sam: I'll file a ticket and include the reproducer script, exact config diffs, and a quick e2e test for the continuous-batcher path.

Alex: Thanks all — closing the immediate escalation. I'll follow up with the customer write-up in 1h. :thumbsup:
